chunks: Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying:
A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم asking him, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Who has a loan?” One of the Muslims said: “I do.”

So he said: “Give him four wasqs of dates,” and he gave him. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and asked him for repayment. So he said: “It will come, and I will give you.” Then he returned, so he said: “It will come, and I will give you.” Then he returned, so he said: “It will come, and I will give you.” Then he said: “You have done much, O Messenger of Allah,” so he laughed.

And he said: “Who has a loan?” So a man stood and said: “I do.” He said: “How much do you have?” He said: “Whatever you wish.” He said: “Give him eight wasqs.” The man said: “I only have four.” He عليه السلام said: “And four more as well.”

key_terms.أَكْثَرْتَ: you have done much or gone to great lengths
key_terms.أَوْسَاقٍ: measured loads; a plural unit of quantity used for dates
key_terms.تَمْرٍ: dates, the commodity mentioned in the loan
key_terms.سَلَفٌ: a loan or advance given to someone

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم handling of a loan and repayment?
ai.summary: This report recounts that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم arranged a loan of dates for a needy man and later ordered a greater amount to be given in settlement. The narration reflects generosity, fulfillment of obligations, and a practical context relevant to discussions of loans and financial dealings. It also highlights the noble character of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in responding to repeated requests with forbearance and grace.
